history.criteriaSummary: GLP-1s (Saxenda, Wegovy, Zepbound) for weight management are conditionally covered for beneficiaries who are overweight or obese and meet specific BMI criteria (e.g., BMI >= 27 kg/m2 with comorbidity, or age-specific BMI percentiles for adolescents). Coverage requires ongoing lifestyle modifications, no combination with other GLP-1s, and no FDA contraindications. Renewal criteria include demonstrating weight loss (e.g., 5% for adults, 4% BMI reduction for adolescents) and continued lifestyle modifications. Initial approval is for 6 months, renewals for 12 months. Quantity limits apply.
history.criteriaVerbatim:
The beneficiary is overweight or obese and is using the requested age

[...]ual to 27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related 
comorbidity/risk factor/complication (i.e. hypertension, type 2 diabetes, 
obstructive sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia) OR 
 The beneficiary is 12 - 17 years of age and has ONE of the following: 
• A BMI greater than or equal to the 95th percentile for age and sex OR 
• A BMI greater than or equal to 30 kg/m2 OR 
• A BMI greater than or equal to the 85th percentile for age and sex AND at least 
one severe weight-related comorbidity/risk factor/complication OR 
 The beneficiary is 45 years of age or older with a BMI greater than or equal to 27 kg/m2 
AND has established cardiovascular disease (CVD) defined as having a history of 
myocardial infarction, stroke, or symptomatic peripheral disease, to be documented on the 
PA form. AND
o The beneficiary is currently on and will continue lifestyle modification including structured 
nutrition and physical activity, unless physical activity is not clinically appropriate at the time 
GLP1 therapy commences.  AND 
o The beneficiary will NOT be using the requested agent in combination with another GLP-1 
receptor agonist agent AND 
o The beneficiary does NOT have any FDA-labeled contraindications to the requested agent,

neoplasia type II.

• The beneficiary has been previously approved for the requested agent through Medicaid’s Prior Authorization

• The beneficiary is using the requested agent for weight management and ALL of the following criteria have

• The beneficiary is continuing a current weight loss course of therapy AND

Baseline and current weight are to be provided on the PA form. OR

Baseline and current weight are to be provided on the PA form. OR

records.criteriaSummary: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Saxenda, Wegovy, Zepbound) are covered with prior authorization. Initial approval requires meeting FDA age limits, documentation of reduced calorie diet or registered dietitian care, increased physical activity (unless contraindicated), and specific baseline BMI criteria (>=30 kg/m2 or >=27 kg/m2 with a weight-related comorbidity for adults; >=30 kg/m2 and >60 kg for ages 12-17). Patient's baseline weight must be submitted. No contraindications should exist unless benefits outweigh risks, and no concurrent use of other weight loss drugs. Initial approval is for 6 months. Renewal requires at least 5% weight loss (or 5% BMI reduction for ages 12-17), ongoing diet/nutritionist care, ongoing physical activity, and no contraindications. Renewal is for 12 months, with subsequent renewals requiring maintenance of weight loss. Quantity limits apply per FDA label.
records.criteriaVerbatim:
Covered drugs with prior authorization:
* Saxenda
* Wegovy
* Zepbound

Initial approval criteria for covered drugs with prior authorization:
* Patient must meet the age limit indicated in the FDA-approved label of the requested drug AND
* Documentation of initiation of or ongoing reduced calorie diet; OR
* Documentation of ongoing care of a registered dietitian nutritionist; AND
* Documentation of initiation of or ongoing regimen of increased physical activity unless medically contraindicated by co-morbidity AND
* Baseline body mass index (BMI) must be:
  + Greater than or equal to 30 kg/m2 with no risk factors (for patient at least 18 years of age) OR
  + Greater than or equal to 27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related comorbid condition (e.g. hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, or dyslipidemia) (for patient at least 18 years of age) OR
  + Greater than or equal to 30 kg/m2 and body weight above 60 kg (for patient 12 to 17 years of age) AND
* Patient’s weight at baseline (in kg) must be submitted at time of request
* No contraindications (disease state or current therapy) should exist unless the prescriber documents that benefits outweigh risks AND
* No concurrent use of any other weight loss drug(s) AND
* Initial approval is for:
  + 6 months for Saxenda, Wegovy, Contrave, Xenical or orlistat; and may be renewed if renewal criteria is met. After lapses of therapy, additional trials may be approved if initial approval criteria is met.

Renewal criteria for covered drugs with prior authorization:
* Patient, at least 18 years of age, must have at least 5% weight loss during the initial approval period OR
* Patient, 12 to 17 years of age, must have at least 5% reduction in baseline BMI during the initial approval period AND
* Documentation of ongoing reduced calorie diet OR
* Documentation of ongoing care of a registered dietitian nutritionist AND
* Documentation of ongoing regimen of increased physical activity unless medically contraindicated by co-morbidity AND
* No contraindications (disease state or current therapy) should exist, unless prescriber documents that benefits outweigh risks AND
* Renewal approval is for 12 months
* Subsequent renewal approval (beyond 18 months) requires meeting all renewal criteria and documentation that patient maintains weight loss achieved during the initial approval period

Quantity limits
Quantity limits pursuant to the FDA-approved label will apply.

Step 1: Lifestyle modification. Before any pharmacotherapy, patients must document participation in a structured lifestyle intervention. Acceptable interventions include enrollment in a weight-loss program (minimum 8 weeks), dietary counseling with a registered dietitian (minimum 3 visits), or a trial of metformin for patients with prediabetes or insulin resistance (minimum 90 days).

Step 2: First-line pharmacotherapy. If lifestyle modification alone doesn't produce clinically significant weight loss (typically defined as 5% of baseline body weight), the patient can try phentermine (for patients without cardiovascular contraindications) or orlistat. Both are generic and cost Illinois Medicaid under $30 per month.

records.criteriaSummary: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Saxenda, Wegovy, Zepbound) are covered with prior authorization. Initial approval requires meeting FDA-approved age limits, documentation of a reduced calorie diet or care from a registered dietitian, and increased physical activity (unless medically contraindicated). Baseline BMI must be >=30 kg/m2 (no risk factors) or >=27 kg/m2 (with at least one weight-related comorbidity) for adults, or >=30 kg/m2 and body weight >60 kg for ages 12-17. Renewal requires at least 5% weight loss (adults) or 5% BMI reduction (ages 12-17), ongoing diet/dietitian care, ongoing physical activity, and no contraindications. Renewal is for 12 months, with subsequent renewals requiring maintenance of weight loss. Quantity limits apply per FDA label.

records.criteriaSummary: Coverage for GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity/weight management is conditional on prior authorization. Typical requirements include BMI thresholds (generally BMI ≥30 or BMI ≥27 with a comorbidity), documentation of comorbidities, proof of previous weight management efforts (e.g., 3–6 month supervised diet and exercise plan), and prior medication history (trials of older weight loss drugs may be required). Re-authorization often requires demonstrating at least 5% weight loss over several months. Coverage for obesity treatment specifically varies by plan, with some plans covering for type 2 diabetes but not obesity. Medicare Part D and Medicaid coverage also varies by state and plan, and some plans may exclude coverage for obesity drugs altogether.
records.criteriaVerbatim:
Most insurance companies set strict medical necessity criteria for GLP-1 weight loss medications. Common requirements include:

### BMI thresholds

Generally, BMI ≥30 or BMI ≥27 with a comorbidity such as hypertension, cardiovascular disease, high cholesterol, or sleep apnea.

### Comorbidity documentation

Your provider must note any health conditions that could improve with weight loss.

### Lifestyle attempts

Proof of previous weight management efforts, such as a 3–6 month supervised diet and exercise plan.

### Prior medication history

Some health plans require trials of older weight loss drugs before approving GLP-1 agonists.

### Preferred drug list adherence

If your plan covers Saxenda but not Wegovy, you may need to try Saxenda first unless there's a clinical reason to skip it.

### Re-authorization criteria

Demonstrating results, often at least 5% weight loss over several months, is important to continue coverage.

While GLP-1 medications are approved for certain conditions, insurance coverage depends on the drug's labeled indication and your plan's formulary. Some health plans cover them for type 2 diabetes (Ozempic, Trulicity, Rybelsus, Victoza) but not for the treatment of obesity (Wegovy, Saxenda, Zepbound, Mounjaro). Medicare Part D and Medicaid coverage also varies by state and plan, making it essential to confirm benefits before starting therapy.

Some insurance plans, including certain Medicare Part D and Medicaid programs, exclude coverage for obesity drugs altogether, making it necessary to ask about plan exceptions or explore patient assistance programs from manufacturers like Novo Nordisk. Others impose step therapy requirements, meaning you must try another drug first unless your provider can justify an exception for medical reasons. Off-label prescribing (such as using Ozempic or Trulicity for weight loss without type 2 diabetes) can also be more difficult to approve, requiring a strong clinical rationale.

history.criteriaSummary: Coverage for GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity/weight management is conditional on prior authorization. Typical requirements include BMI thresholds (generally BMI ≥30 or BMI ≥27 with a comorbidity), documentation of comorbidities, proof of previous weight management efforts (e.g., 3–6 month supervised diet and exercise plan), and prior medication history (trials of older weight loss drugs may be required). Re-authorization often requires demonstrating at least 5% weight loss over several months. Coverage for obesity treatment specifically varies by plan, with some plans covering for type 2 diabetes but not obesity. Medicare Part D and Medicaid coverage also varies by state and plan, and some plans may exclude coverage for obesity drugs altogether.
history.criteriaVerbatim:
Most insurance companies set strict medical necessity criteria for GLP-1 weight loss medications. Common requirements include:

### BMI thresholds

Generally, BMI ≥30 or BMI ≥27 with a comorbidity such as hypertension, cardiovascular disease, high cholesterol, or sleep apnea.

### Comorbidity documentation

Your provider must note any health conditions that could improve with weight loss.

### Lifestyle attempts

Proof of previous weight management efforts, such as a 3–6 month supervised diet and exercise plan.

### Prior medication history

Some health plans require trials of older weight loss drugs before approving GLP-1 agonists.

### Preferred drug list adherence

If your plan covers Saxenda but not Wegovy, you may need to try Saxenda first unless there's a clinical reason to skip it.

### Re-authorization criteria

Demonstrating results, often at least 5% weight loss over several months, is important to continue coverage.

While GLP-1 medications are approved for certain conditions, insurance coverage depends on the drug's labeled indication and your plan's formulary. Some health plans cover them for type 2 diabetes (Ozempic, Trulicity, Rybelsus, Victoza) but not for the treatment of obesity (Wegovy, Saxenda, Zepbound, Mounjaro). Medicare Part D and Medicaid coverage also varies by state and plan, making it essential to confirm benefits before starting therapy.

Some insurance plans, including certain Medicare Part D and Medicaid programs, exclude coverage for obesity drugs altogether, making it necessary to ask about plan exceptions or explore patient assistance programs from manufacturers like Novo Nordisk. Others impose step therapy requirements, meaning you must try another drug first unless your provider can justify an exception for medical reasons. Off-label prescribing (such as using Ozempic or Trulicity for weight loss without type 2 diabetes) can also be more difficult to approve, requiring a strong clinical rationale.

All drugs in the hypoglycemics, GLP-1 drug class are diagnosis restricted. A ForwardHealth-allowed diagnosis code must be indicated on claims (and PA requests when applicable) for all drugs in the hypoglycemics, GLP-1 drug class.

Clinical criteria for approval of a PA request for a non-preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agent are all of the following:
* The non-preferred drug is being prescribed in a manner consistent with the FDA-approved product labeling.
* The member has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
* The member's HbA1c was measured within the past six months.
* If the member is not currently using a hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agent, their most recent HbA1c is 6.5% or greater.

One of the following must be documented for at least two of the preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agents:
* The member has taken the maximum dose of a preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agent for at least three consecutive months and experienced an unsatisfactory therapeutic response in glycemic control. (Note: Initial PA requests require an HbA1c measurement after the member has been taking the maximum dose of a preferred agent for at least three consecutive months.)
* The member experienced a clinically significant adverse drug reaction with a preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agent.

PA requests for non-preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agents may be initially approved for up to 183 days.

Renewal PA requests may be approved for up to 365 days if the member has been adherent with the prescribed treatment regimen and had a reduction in their HbA1c compared to their baseline prior to the initiation of the non-preferred hypoglycemics, GLP-1 agent.
